answer: src/click/core.py, the `Parameter.spec` property (base class; spec = max(opts, key=len of _split_opt prefix), falls back to name if no opts). Option has no own spec override per the doc. But spec must agree with name, so Option._parse_decls (possible_names sort, longest prefix, stable) must change consistently or test_spec in tests/test_options.py fails.

src/click/core.py, Argument class: `Argument.get_help_spec(ctx)` (returns make_metavar(ctx), e.g. [FILENAME]...) decides the left column (get_help_record routes through it), and `Argument.get_error_hint` uses get_help_spec(ctx) when ctx is present, else `Argument.spec` (metavar or name.upper()). Change those (or Argument.spec / make_metavar).

src/click/core.py, `Parameter.__init_subclass__`: checks `'human_readable_name' in cls.__dict__` and warns DeprecationWarning with stacklevel=_outside_click_stacklevel(skip=("abc",)). The line it points at is controlled by `_outside_click_stacklevel` (its skip argument added by this PR); the doc doesn't say which module it lives in - guess src/click/_utils.py or core.py/utils.py.

At import (class definition) time, Parameter.__init_subclass__ emits a DeprecationWarning: "MyOpt overrides 'human_readable_name'. Click no longer reads that property. Override 'spec' instead. Click will remove 'human_readable_name' in 9.0.", attributed to the plugin's class line. At runtime click ignores the override: messages/help/error hints use spec (e.g. '--my-opt'), so 'custom' is never shown by click. Only code that reads .human_readable_name directly on the instance gets 'custom' (the override replaces the warning property, so no read warning).

Now: "DeprecationWarning: The option '--my-option' is deprecated." Before: "DeprecationWarning: The option 'my_option' is deprecated." (echoed, not just warnings.warn). click.Option(['-t','--times']).human_readable_name emits a DeprecationWarning and returns '--times' (was 'times').

Options: tests/test_options.py (test_spec, test_spec_with_explicit_name, test_deprecated_warning). Arguments: tests/test_arguments.py (test_spec_and_help_spec, test_help_spec_matches_help_record). Run option spec tests: `tox -e py3.13 -- tests/test_options.py -k spec` (or with a venv: `pytest tests/test_options.py -k spec`).

tests/test_deprecations.py (test_parameter_human_readable_name_deprecated, test_parameter_human_readable_name_override_deprecated, test_parameter_subclass_without_override_is_silent). Run: `pytest tests/test_deprecations.py -k human_readable_name` (or tox -e py3.13 -- tests/test_deprecations.py). A bare read fails because the property emits DeprecationWarning and the test suite presumably turns warnings into errors (filterwarnings = error in pytest config) - not in doc, guess on the config detail.

Fixing in place would silently change the return value of a public property (options would go from 'my_option' to '--my-option') and click would keep honoring subclass overrides of an ambiguously-named thing; a new clearly named `spec` gives an override point plus a deprecation path (read warns, override warns at class definition) to removal in 9.0. Note it still does change the return value to spec, documented in CHANGES/upgrade guide. Longest-prefix: it's the same rule Option._parse_decls uses to derive `name`, so spec is exactly the declaration name came from (invariant tested: _split_opt(spec)[1].replace('-','_').lower()==name), and the long form (--times) is the most descriptive spelling for users. Exact maintainer rationale for new-property-vs-in-place beyond this is partly a guess.
